first_impression.reaction: I Googled this because I'm trying to work out whether I even want a bridal party, and half our friends would have to fly. The first line is sensible, not gushy: 'Because a wedding is easier, and happier, with people you trust beside you.' What kept me going was the roadmap promising 'how many to ask, bridesmen, and asking friends to travel'. That last bit is my real question, so I skimmed down to find it.

journey.quote: For a wedding abroad, ask attendants early and talk openly about travel, time off and who covers what before anyone books.
journey.reaction: Good, the takeaways admit money is part of this. That's the awkward conversation I've been avoiding.

journey.section: 1. Why do we have bridesmaids today?
journey.quote: Many couples now choose attendants by closeness, not convention.
journey.reaction: Yes. James wants his sister on my side and I want my oldest friend, who's a guy. Nice to see that treated as normal straight away.

journey.section: 1. Why do we have bridesmaids today?
journey.quote: "Always a bridesmaid, never a bride" goes back to the 1880s, and the "often a bridesmaid" version spread through mouthwash advertisements from the 1920s.
journey.reaction: The mouthwash detail made me laugh, I'll use that at the hens. But four dates in one paragraph and I was already skimming.

journey.quote: In classical Athens, women attended wedding feasts where bridesmaids danced.
journey.reaction: Fine, but Athens and Rome don't help me decide anything. I scrolled past this to Victoria.

journey.section: 3. Queen Victoria's bridesmaids and royal attendants
journey.quote: A long train or cathedral veil needs one or two named attendants, briefed and rehearsed on the actual aisle, steps and turns of your ceremony venue.
journey.reaction: This is the kind of detail I want. Turning a dull history fact into a run-sheet job. Someone's actually stood at the back of a chapel abroad.

journey.section: 5 and 6. Matching dresses and how many
journey.quote: Victoria had twelve, and nineteenth-century parties of eight or twelve were common, but a single attendant is just as complete.
journey.reaction: By now Victoria's twelve has come up in the takeaways, section 3, section 5 and here. I got it the first time.

journey.section: 4. Maid of honour or matron of honour
journey.quote: So the difference is marriage, not rank.
journey.reaction: Clear and quick. That's settled an argument with my mum.

journey.section: 6. How many bridesmaids should you have?
journey.quote: At a destination wedding, every attendant is a guest making a real commitment.
journey.reaction: Honest trade-off. This is why I'm thinking three, not seven.

journey.quote: Asking someone to be a bridesmaid abroad is asking for their leave, their travel and several days of their year.
journey.reaction: Best line on the page for us. It's exactly what I've been feeling and not saying. Sending this section to James.

journey.quote: Who covers flights and accommodation, and is that the same for every attendant?
journey.reaction: The 'same for every attendant' bit is smart. One of my friends earns a lot less than the others and I hadn't thought about how that would play.

journey.quote: Each attendant checks their own passport is valid for at least six months beyond the end of the trip, and their own visa for every country they visit or transit through.
journey.reaction: Practical, and it makes clear whose job it is. The lawyer in me likes that responsibility is spelled out.

journey.quote: One contact. Name one person the venue team can reach about the party's timings.
journey.reaction: One person from where, though? Is that meant to be my maid of honour, or the Wedded Advisor? I don't want my best friend running logistics in a foreign language on the morning. This is my 'who's accountable' worry again.

journey.quote: One advisor is your single point of contact, works in your time zone and confirms inclusions in writing.
journey.reaction: Single point of contact and 'in writing' both land with me. Low-key, not pushy, and it comes right after the section where I'd actually want help.

journey.quote: Pair it with a handwritten note that names one thing each person did.
journey.reaction: Lovely and not twee. Better than another monogrammed robe.

journey.quote: A sibling or friend can still hold the rings and sign as a witness where the ceremony allows.
journey.reaction: 'Where the ceremony allows' makes me twitch. If we go small with no attendants, how many witnesses does it need to be legal, and can a friend from Sydney sign? I'd want that answered somewhere.

journey.quote: Your advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: Quoting in AUD goes straight at my currency worry. Good.

unanswered_questions: Who is the 'one contact' on the ground for the wedding party: the Wedded Advisor, someone local you're accountable for, or one of our attendants?
Is the Wedded Advisor, or someone you answer for, physically there on the morning and at the ceremony?
If we have no attendants, what are the witness rules for a legal ceremony abroad, and can overseas friends act as witnesses?
Can you help organise travel and accommodation for the wedding party, or do attendants book their own?
Is there a real wedding, with venue and date, showing how a travelling bridal party was looked after?
would_share_with: James: section 9, especially 'asking for their leave, their travel and several days of their year' and the questions to talk through
My mum: the maid versus matron of honour section ('the difference is marriage, not rank')
My maid of honour, once asked: the before and on-the-day duties list and the Smartraveller paragraph

cta_reaction.why: No hard sell, and AUD quotes plus a written fee are reassuring. But I came for a bridesmaid question and haven't picked a country. I'd read a destination post and a real wedding before I'd talk to anyone.

top_3_changes: Say plainly who the 'one contact' is on the ground, so the destination section answers the accountability question instead of quietly handing it to a bridesmaid.
Cut the repeated 'Victoria had twelve' references after section 3; four mentions reads like padding to a skimmer.
Trim the proverb dates in section 1 and the Athens and Rome lines so a skimmer reaches the practical sections (how many, duties, destination) faster.

open_questions.question: This is an early-funnel tradition search, so a low likelihood_to_enquire is expected for this persona. Should it be weighted with that in mind?

Read the full draft once, skimming the proverb dates, Athens and Rome, and the 1903 costume paragraph as Sophie would.
Family and friend details (James's sister, a male best friend, a friend on a lower income) are persona colour, not brand facts.
